//: The verification record behind data/suppliers.json. Nothing renders this file.
It exists because the page tells the reader every shop was checked by hand, and a
claim like that should have something behind it. It is also what stops the next
person re-researching the same twenty-five dead ends: two of the rejections below
are shops a plausible-looking domain would have got wrong.
Re-verify before trusting a date older than a year. Shops in this trade close, and
a directory of dead links is worse than no directory.

Rejections record that we could not VERIFY a shop on the date shown. They are not findings about the business, and a transient failure says nothing durable — recheck before treating any of them as settled.
method: Each URL was fetched and its page read to confirm the business sells classic Mini parts. Sites that refused an automated request were re-fetched by other means and the page text quoted below. A site that could not be read at all was rejected rather than guessed at.
